Loaded Sheet Pan Shredded Chicken Nachos Recipe

These sheet pan chicken nachos have everything I want in a pan of nachos: crunchy tortilla chips, saucy shredded chicken, refried beans, lots of melty cheese, and enough fresh toppings to keep every bite interesting. And because we’re starting with store-bought rotisserie chicken, the whole thing comes together in about 20 minutes.

Which is excellent news because nachos are usually something I want immediately.

You know the feeling.

The Secret to Better Sheet Pan Nachos

The trick is simple: layer everything. I build these sheet pan nachos in two layers so the saucy chicken, refried beans, cheddar, and Monterey Jack make it onto more than just the top chips.

The chicken gets tossed with salsa for easy flavor, and the two cheeses give you plenty of melty goodness.

Then I finish the whole thing with cotija or queso fresco, guacamole, red onion, pickled jalapeños, and sour cream.  

I use the same sheet-pan approach in these Chicken Fajita Nachos, another easy option when you’re feeding a crowd.

Why Real California Milk Makes Better Nachos

Nachos are not the time to be shy about dairy. The cheese is one of the main reasons we’re all here.

I’m using Real California Milk  cheddar cheese, Monterey Jack cheese, and sour cream in this recipe. Look for the Real California Milk seal at the grocery store—it lets you know the dairy was made with milk from California dairy farm families.

I especially love the combination of the hot, melty cheese with cold sour cream spooned over the top. It’s rich and creamy, a little messy, and exactly what nachos should be.

What You’ll Need for Shredded Chicken Nachos

Saucy Shredded Chicken

  • Rotisserie Chicken – Leftover cooked chicken works just as well if that’s what you have.
  • Red Salsa – Use your favorite red salsa; salsa verde is an easy swap.

For the Nachos

  • Tortilla Chips – Use a bag of sturdy tortilla chips because flimsy chips and loaded nachos are not a good match.
  • Refried Beans – Adds creamy texture and makes every layer more satisfying.
  • Real California Milk Cheddar and Monterey Jack Cheese – Give you the best mix of sharp flavor and serious meltiness; a Mexican cheese blend works in a pinch.

Favorite Toppings

  • Real California Milk Cotija or Queso Fresco – Adds a salty punch while queso fresco is softer and milder, and both are usually easy to find near the Mexican cheeses.
  • Red Onion – Adds crunch and a sharp bite that cuts through all that cheese; green onions are a good backup.
  • Guacamole – brings cool, creamy richness to the whole situation, and store-bought is absolutely fine when you want to keep things easy.
  • Real California Milk Sour Cream – Adds a cool, tangy finish that balances the hot, cheesy nachos; plain Greek yogurt works in a pinch.
  • Pickled Jalapeños – Add tangy heat and are usually found near the pickles or Mexican foods; fresh jalapeños work if you want a brighter, sharper bite.

How To Make Sheet Pan Chicken Nachos

1. Make the Saucy Shredded Chicken. Place the shredded chicken in a large bowl and toss with the salsa until every piece is coated in a saucy chicken mixture.

2. Prep the Baking Sheet. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper for easy cleanup and to keep the bottom layer of chips from sticking.

3. Build the First Layer. Spread half of the tortilla chips over the baking sheet in a single layer. Scatter half of the  beans, half of the shredded cheese, and half of the shredded chicken mixture evenly over the chips.

4. Add a Second Layer. Add the remaining chips in an even layer, then top with the rest of the beans, chicken mixture and the remaining shredded cheese.

5. Bake Until the Cheese Melts. Bake for 10-12 minutes, until the cheese melts completely and turns bubbly at the edges. 

6. Top and Serve. Pull the pan from the oven and immediately scatter on your favorite nacho toppings: cotija, red onion, dollops of guacamole, and definitely dollops of sour cream. Serve the entire platter right away, while the chips are still crispy tortilla chips and the cheese is at its meltiest.

What Cheese Is Best for Nachos?

I like a mix of cheddar cheese and Monterey Jack cheese. Cheddar brings the flavor and Monterey Jack melts beautifully. A Mexican cheese blend works too, and pre-shredded cheeses are totally fine if that’s what you have.

Finish with cotija cheese or queso fresco for a little extra salty flavor.

If you love experimenting with different cheeses, these Sweet Potato Nachos with Smoked Cheddar are another favorite and a great example of how much the cheese can change the whole pan.

Easy Chicken Nacho Variations

Nachos are very forgiving, so don’t be afraid to change things up.

For a meatless version, take a cue from my Oven-Roasted Veggie Fajita Nachos and load the chips with roasted vegetables instead of chicken.

You can also add black beans, pinto beans, black olives, green onions, fresh pico de gallo, or avocado.

What to Serve with Chicken Nachos

These nachos are filling enough on their own, but if you’re making a bigger spread, a few extras never hurt.

  • Tacos or quesadillas if you’re feeding a crowd
  • Mexican street corn for something sweet, smoky, and cheesy
  • Mexican rice or cilantro-lime rice to round out dinner
  • Chicken wings and Mexican red fries for game day or a party

These sheet pan chicken nachos are great for football season, movie night, or an easy dinner when chips and cheese sound better than everything else.

And nachos don’t have to wait until later in the day either. My Loaded Sweet Potato Breakfast Nachos with Margarita Salsa are proof that breakfast nachos are absolutely a thing.

Storage

Nachos are best fresh. Store leftover nachos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days, although the chips will soften.

For best results, store extra chicken mixture separately for up to 3 days, then make a fresh batch of nachos next time.

FAQs

Can I make chicken nachos ahead of time?

Prep the chicken, cheese, and toppings ahead, but wait to assemble and bake the nachos until just before serving.

Can I use leftover chicken?

Yes. You need 3 cups cooked shredded chicken.

Can I use black beans instead of refried beans?

Absolutely. Black beans or pinto beans both work.

How do I keep nachos from getting soggy?

Use sturdy tortilla chips, don’t pile the layers too high, add wet toppings (like salsa) after baking, and serve right away.

Sheet Pan Shredded Chicken Nachos Recipe

If you’re looking for shredded chicken nacho recipes that are easy enough for dinner but still feel like you’ve made something really fun, this is the one.
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 30 minutes mins
Cook Time 10 minutes mins
Total Time 40 minutes mins
Servings: 8 servings
Course: Appetizer
Cuisine: Mexican-American
Ingredients Equipment Method Notes

Ingredients
  

  • 3 cups shredded store-bought rotisserie chicken, leftover chicken works too
  • 1 cup your favorite red salsa or salsa verde
  • 1 16-ounce bag sturdy tortilla chips
  • 1 15-ounce can refried beans or 2 cups homemade refried beans
  • 2 cups Real California Milk shredded cheddar cheese
  • 2 cups Real California Milk shredded Monterey Jack cheese
Favorite Toppings
  • Real California Milk cotija cheese or queso fresco
  • thinly sliced red onion
  • Guacamole, store-bought or homemade
  • Real California Milk sour cream
  • pickled jalapeño slices

Equipment

  • box grater
  • mixing bowl
  • baking sheet
  • measuring cups

Method
 

  1. Make the Saucy Shredded Chicken: Place the 3 cups shredded chicken in a large bowl and toss with the 1 cup salsa until every piece is coated in a saucy chicken mixture.
  2. Prep the Baking Sheet: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper for easy cleanup and to keep the bottom layer of chips from sticking.
  3. Build the First Layer: Spread half of the tortilla chips over the baking sheet in a single layer. Scatter half of the beans, half of the shredded cheese, and half of the shredded chicken mixture evenly over the chips.
  4. Add a Second Layer: Add the remaining chips in an even layer, then top with the rest of the beans, chicken mixture and the remaining shredded cheese.
  5. Bake Until the Cheese Melts: Bake for 10-12 minutes, until the cheese melts completely and turns bubbly at the edges.
  6. Top and Serve: Pull the pan from the oven and immediately scatter on your favorite nacho toppings: cotija, red onion, dollops of guacamole, and definitely dollops of sour cream. Serve the entire platter right away, while the chips are still crispy tortilla chips and the cheese is at its meltiest.

Notes

  1. Storage: Nachos are always best fresh, but leftover nachos can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days — the chips will soften, so this is really more about saving the chicken mixture. For best results, store any extra saucy shredded chicken separately in an airtight container and make fresh nachos next time rather than reheating the whole platter.
  2. From-scratch option: Prefer to cook your own chicken? Season 1 pound skinless chicken breasts with 1 teaspoon chili powder and 1 teaspoon garlic powder and 1 teaspoon kosher salt, then place chicken in a large skillet with a little olive oil over medium-low heat and cook until the internal temperature reaches 165°F. Shred with two forks and toss with the salsa and a little lime juice. A slow cooker chicken version works too: cook the seasoned raw chicken breasts on low for 6-8 hours, lift out with a slotted spoon, shred, and stir into the salsa — a great way to get the chicken ahead of time if you’re planning a game day spread.
  3. BBQ chicken nachos variation: Swap the red salsa for your favorite BBQ sauce and use cheddar and Monterey Jack cheese as the base for classic bbq chicken nachos.
  4. Buffalo chicken nachos variation: Toss the shredded chicken in buffalo sauce instead of red salsa for a spicy twist, and finish with an extra dollop of sour cream to cool things down.
